title: Batch and Streaming K-Means Clustering with a C Backend
text: R package implementing batch streaming k-means clustering core computations written C via R native API.

title: Batch and Streaming K-Means Clustering with a C Backend
text: stReans provides two complementary approaches k-means clustering: kmeans_batch() - Lloyd’s algorithm datasets fit memory, convergence detection based centroid shift kmeans_stream() - incremental online k-means data streams, processing one observation time without storing full dataset (coming soon)

title: Batch and Streaming K-Means Clustering with a C Backend
Batch and Streaming K-Means Clustering with a C Backend
code: library(stReans)  # generate three well-separated clusters set.seed(42) cluster1 <- matrix(rnorm(40, mean = 0,  sd = 0.5), nrow = 20) cluster2 <- matrix(rnorm(40, mean = 5,  sd = 0.5), nrow = 20) cluster3 <- matrix(rnorm(40, mean = 10, sd = 0.5), nrow = 20) X <- rbind(cluster1, cluster2, cluster3)  # run batch k-means result <- kmeans_batch(X, k = 3L, max_iter = 100L, tol = 1e-6)  result$centers      # cluster centroids result$assignments  # cluster label per observation result$iterations   # how many iterations ran

Batch K-Means Clustering — kmeans_batch
text: X numeric matrix row observation k positive integer, number clusters max_iter positive integer, maximum number iterations (default = 100) tol positive numeric, convergance tolerance centroids shift (default = 1e-6)

title: Batch K-Means Clustering — kmeans_batch
text: list two components: 'centers': matrix clustering centroids (dim: k x ncol(X)) 'assignments': integer vector clustering labels (1-indexed) 'iterations': integer number completed iterations

title: Batch K-Means Clustering — kmeans_batch
code: # simple 2D example with three well-separated clusters set.seed(42) cluster1 <- matrix(rnorm(40, mean = 0,  sd = 0.5), nrow = 20) cluster2 <- matrix(rnorm(40, mean = 5,  sd = 0.5), nrow = 20) cluster3 <- matrix(rnorm(40, mean = 10, sd = 0.5), nrow = 20) X <- rbind(cluster1, cluster2, cluster3) X <- X[sample(nrow(X)),] # for better initial centers result <- kmeans_batch(X, k = 3L, max_iter = 100L, tol = 1e-6) #> iter 1: shift = 0.6887 #>   center 1: (0.0960, -0.1355) #>   center 2: (10.0410, 10.0077) #>   center 3: (4.9995, 5.0803) #> iter 2: shift = 0.0000 #>   center 1: (0.0960, -0.1355) #>   center 2: (10.0410, 10.0077) #>   center 3: (4.9995, 5.0803) result$centers #>             [,1]       [,2] #> [1,]  0.09596001 -0.1354959 #> [2,] 10.04097793 10.0076688 #> [3,]  4.99954464  5.0803004 result$assignments #>  [1] 1 2 3 3 2 3 1 1 2 1 2 1 3 1 2 3 3 1 2 1 1 1 3 2 1 2 2 2 1 1 3 1 3 3 1 1 2 3 #> [39] 3 1 2 2 2 3 3 3 2 2 1 3 2 1 1 3 3 2 2 2 3 3 result$iterations #> [1] 2  # plot the result plot(X[, 1], X[, 2],      col = result$assignments,      pch = 16, cex = 1.5,      xlab = "X1", ylab = "X2",      main = "Batch K-Means") points(result$centers[, 1], result$centers[, 2],        col = 1:3, pch = 4, cex = 3, lwd = 3)
